name: org.machanism.machai:mcp-server-maven-plugin
description: MCP Server Maven Plugin is a Java 17 Apache Maven plugin that runs a Machai Model Context Protocol (MCP) server from a Maven build, avoiding a separate server launcher or manually assembled runtime command. Its aggregator goals start one HTTP server for a Maven reactor: stateless selects the stateless HTTP transport and streamable selects the streamable HTTP transport. Both goals use the current Maven project name, version, and base directory; load Machai server and tool settings through a PropertiesConfigurator; configure the listening port and project directory; register configured AI tools; and start the selected MCP server. An optional parameter map is copied to JVM system properties only when a property has not already been supplied, preserving process-level overrides. The plugin is intended for local AI-assisted development, repeatable integration tests, demonstrations, and build-driven automation. MCP clients consume the configured tools over HTTP, and the supplied lifecycle function can request an orderly delayed JVM exit after a workflow completes. Configuration and startup problems are reported as Maven execution errors.

constructors.description: Creates the lifecycle function-tools component that exposes controlled MCP server shutdown to a running Machai MCP server.

examples.description: In an embedded Java integration, create the lifecycle tool and request normal termination. In standard plugin operation, server configuration registers the tool rather than application code creating it directly.

features.name: stateless
features.description: Starts a stateless HTTP MCP server as an aggregator Maven goal. It applies configured parameters, loads the MCP configuration, initializes the server from Maven project metadata, sets its project directory and HTTP port, registers configured tools, and starts the endpoint.

examples.description: Step 1: add the plugin to the consuming Maven build, or use its fully specified coordinates. Step 2: create a readable MCP properties file with Machai server and tool settings. Step 3: run the stateless goal with a port and configuration location. Step 4: while Maven remains running, connect an MCP-compatible HTTP client to the configured endpoint.

features.name: streamable
features.description: Starts a streamable HTTP MCP server as an aggregator Maven goal. It performs the common Maven project, configuration, parameter, base-directory, port, and tool-registration processing, then selects the streamable HTTP transport.

examples.description: Step 1: install or resolve the ready-to-use plugin by invoking its fully specified Maven coordinates. Step 2: provide a readable Machai MCP configuration and an available HTTP port. Step 3: run the streamable goal. Step 4: configure the MCP client to use the resulting streamable HTTP endpoint.

features.name: stopMcpServer
features.description: Initiates an orderly delayed MCP server shutdown, records final usage statistics, and exits the JVM with the supplied exit code. The MCP function defaults its exit-code argument to 0 for normal completion. This function tool is supported for McpServer.

examples.description: After an MCP client completes a local development or test workflow, invoke the registered stop-mcp-server function with exit-code 0. The server acknowledges the request, waits briefly for the response to complete, records usage, and terminates normally.

customizations.name: mcp.port
customizations.description: Required Maven property that defines the HTTP listening port for either server transport.

examples.description: Supply an available port when starting the stateless server. Use the same property for the streamable goal.

customizations.name: mcp.config
customizations.description: Maven property identifying the readable MCP server configuration file used to load Machai server and tool settings. Supply it for server startup.

examples.description: Pass the configuration file location at invocation time to keep environment-specific settings outside the project POM.

customizations.name: params
customizations.description: Optional map of additional values copied to JVM system properties only when the corresponding system property is not already present.

examples.title: Run a local stateless MCP endpoint
steps: Add org.machanism.machai:mcp-server-maven-plugin:1.4.0 to the Maven build, or invoke the plugin directly by its Maven coordinates.
Prepare an mcp.properties file containing the Machai MCP server and tool configuration.
Connect an MCP-compatible HTTP client to the configured endpoint and use the registered tools while Maven is running.
When the workflow is complete, invoke stop-mcp-server with exit-code 0 for orderly shutdown.

examples.title: Run a streamable HTTP server for a Maven reactor
steps: Run the plugin from the desired Maven project or reactor root so its aggregator goal represents the build rather than each module.
Provide an MCP properties file and select an available port.
Point a streamable HTTP MCP client at the started server and complete the requested tool workflow.
Request shutdown through stop-mcp-server after client work is finished.
